goldens.comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.

The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed.js and embed.css.scss are not added to the asset precompile list, so they are not served in production, causing stylesheet 404 and unstyled iframes

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces new standalone assets `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` and `app/assets/stylesheets/embed.css.scss` and the new layout `app/views/layouts/embed.html.erb` references them via `stylesheet_link_tag 'embed'` (and the embed feature presumably needs `embed.js` to be served too). The diff does not add these files to any asset precompile configuration, and under the default Rails/Sprockets behavior only `application.js`/`application.css` are precompiled (additional JS/CSS entrypoints must be explicitly added). That can lead to 404s / missing styling in production for the embed iframe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Gemfile.lock (Rails 3 lockfile) is not regenerated after adding ruby-readability and simple-rss gems, breaking bundle install and raising LoadError on the Rails 3 build

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `gem 'ruby-readability'` and `gem 'simple-rss'` to `Gemfile` and updates `Gemfile_rails4.lock` accordingly, but there is no corresponding update to the Rails 3 lockfile (`Gemfile.lock` is not touched in this diff). If the Rails 3 build uses `Gemfile.lock`, it would be out of sync with the Gemfile and could break bundling/load (as the finding states).

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:32 uses i.content which is nil/undefined for RSS 2.0 feeds (body is in description), crashing the poll job and aborting the entire feed import with retry: false, so RSS feeds never import

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the job sets `content = CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` (line ~32). If `i.content` is `nil` for any feed item, calling `nil.scrub` will raise `NoMethodError`, crashing the job. Since `sidekiq_options retry: false` is set, this failure would prevent further imports until the next scheduled run, and may effectively block importing for feeds whose items don't populate `content` (e.g., if the parser uses a different field like `description`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embed loading path has no failure state: retrieval failures (throttling, unset embed_by_username, non-http URLs, job errors) leave embed consumers in an infinite 30s reload loop with no diagnostics

adjudication.rationale: In EmbedController#best, when no existing TopicEmbed is found it always enqueues Jobs::RetrieveTopic and renders `embed/loading` (which does a `document.location.reload()` every 30s) with no alternative path. The retrieval job can legitimately be a no-op or fail in diff-grounded ways: TopicRetriever#retrieve skips `perform_retrieve` when `invalid_host?` or `retrieved_recently?` is true; `fetch_http` returns if `embed_by_username` is unset/unknown (user.blank?); and `TopicEmbed.import_remote` / feed polling use `open(...)` without any rescue, so exceptions can abort the job. In these cases no TopicEmbed is created, so subsequent requests keep rendering the loading page, resulting in an indefinite reload loop with no failure state/diagnostics.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_controller.rb:15 TopicView.new is not guarded for deleted/missing/disallowed topics, returning a 500 inside the customer's iframe instead of falling back to loading/error

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns an id, the code directly calls `TopicView.new(topic_id, current_user, {best: 5})` without checking that the topic still exists or is viewable by `current_user` (often `nil` in an embed). Since `topic_id_for_embed` is a raw `pluck` on `topic_embeds`, a stale `topic_id` (e.g., topic deleted) or a restricted topic could plausibly cause `TopicView.new` to raise and produce an ungraceful error in the iframe. The diff shows no rescue/fallback path for this case and no spec covering it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus.thor silently deletes the -c/--category import option with no replacement, so Disqus imports lose category placement and crash with 'Unknown option' when passed

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed, along with the logic that looked up `category_id` from `options[:category]` and passed it into `PostCreator` as `category: category_id`. The import now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)` with no category argument. As a result, any existing usage passing `-c/--category` will fail with Thor's unknown option error, and there is no longer any mechanism in this task to place imported topics into a specified category.

adjudication_records.issue_text: topic_embed.rb:29-33 content_sha1 is updated even when the revision fails, permanently losing the update and making embeds diverge from source forever

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, when an existing embed’s content changes, it calls `revisor.revise!(...)` and then unconditionally runs `embed.update_column(:content_sha1, content_sha1)` (see the `else` branch in `app/models/topic_embed.rb` after `if content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`). If `revise!` returns `false` (it can early-return `false` in `PostRevisor#revise!` when `should_revise?` is not met, and `update_post` uses `save` which can fail without raising), the SHA1 would still be updated even though the post body may not have been updated, causing the embed to stop attempting future updates and diverge from the source.

adjudication_records.issue_text: post.rb:132-134 raw_html posts silently skip the after_post_cook plugin filter chain, an undocumented behavioral contract change

adjudication.rationale: In `Post#cook`, the new early return `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (post.rb) bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` entirely for `raw_html` posts. This is a real, diff-grounded behavioral change that can affect plugins relying on the `:after_post_cook` hook; the diff does not document or mitigate that compatibility impact beyond an inline comment about skipping the rendering pipeline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: poll_feed.rb:19-21 feed_key is dead code: the 'only poll when feed modified' requirement was designed but never implemented, so feeds are re-fetched/re-parsed every hour

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` (lines ~19-21) is defined but never referenced anywhere in the diff, so it is dead/unused code. Also, `poll_feed` unconditionally does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` each time it runs (hourly), with no conditional check against a stored modified timestamp/etag despite the presence of `feed_key`, so it will re-fetch/re-parse on every scheduled execution when enabled. This is a real, diff-grounded inefficiency/incomplete implementation rather than a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed/best.html.erb:16,20 calls post.user.small_avatar_url/username without nil check, crashing the embed view when a post author was deleted

adjudication.rationale: In the new embed view (app/views/embed/best.html.erb), it unconditionally dereferences `post.user` (`post.user.small_avatar_url` and `post.user.username`). The diff doesn’t show guarantees that `post.user` can never be nil (nor does it show deletion behavior), so the specific claim about “deleted authors” isn’t verifiable from the diff. However, the assumption is a concrete, diff-grounded robustness/edge-case concern for a newly introduced view.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import_remote and embed JavaScript have zero test coverage in this diff

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial logic in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (uses `open(url).read` and `Readability::Document.new(...)` to extract title/content) but the new specs only cover `TopicEmbed.import` (`spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`) and do not invoke `import_remote`. Likewise, the newly added client embed script `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js` has no associated JS test/spec in the diff. So the statement that these additions have zero test coverage is supported by what’s shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: absolutize_urls protocol-relative URL handling mangles scheme-relative hrefs (//cdn.example/x) into http://host/cdn.example/x, destroying the URL

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.absolutize_urls`, any `href`/`src` that `start_with?('/')` is rewritten as `"#{prefix}/#{href.sub(/^\/+/, '')}"` (same for `src`). This condition matches protocol-relative URLs like `//cdn.example/x`. The `sub(/^\/+/, '')` strips both leading slashes, producing `cdn.example/x`, and then prefixes it with the article host (e.g., `http://eviltrout.com/cdn.example/x`), which mangles and breaks the original scheme-relative URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unrelated modification to disqus.thor removes the -c/--category option, breaking operators' existing import commands and silently defaulting categories

adjudication.rationale: In lib/tasks/disqus.thor the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` is removed, along with the logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). The import now calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])` without any category parameter, so existing `disqus:import -c <category>` commands will fail due to an unknown option and the imported topics can no longer be assigned to an operator-specified category (effectively defaulting wherever `PostCreator`/TopicEmbed chooses).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import loses original post timestamps because TopicEmbed.import_remote accepts no created_at option

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the thread/topic creation changed from `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]) ...)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` only forwards `opts[:title]` and extracted content to `TopicEmbed.import`, and `TopicEmbed.import` calls `PostCreator.new` without any `created_at` option. Since `PostCreator` only sets `post.created_at` when `@opts[:created_at]` is present (`lib/post_creator.rb`), the imported topic will get the current timestamp instead of the original Disqus thread timestamp—i.e., data loss of timestamps introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding force: true to the pre-existing top_topics migration can silently drop existing table data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration to `create_table :top_topics, force: true`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which could cause data loss if this migration is ever re-run or executed against a DB where `top_topics` already exists. However, for normal upgrades `db:migrate` will not re-run an already-applied migration, so this is a risk/maintenance concern rather than a guaranteed defect introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Whitespace-only churn in migrate_word_counts.rb adds unrelated diff noise

adjudication.rationale: The diff in `db/migrate/20131210181901_migrate_word_counts.rb` is purely whitespace/formatting (removing trailing spaces and adjusting the final newline). While it does add minor diff noise, it does not introduce or expose a functional issue, and per the rubric this is a style/format nit rather than an important review concern.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Embedding admin locale/settings shipped inert: new site settings are server-only with no admin UI, making the embed system unreachable without manual console intervention

adjudication.rationale: The diff does add the new embedding settings to `config/site_settings.yml` under a new `embedding:` group, includes server-side locale strings describing each setting in `config/locales/server.en.yml`, and adds the admin category label `embedding: "Embedding"` in `config/locales/client.en.yml` for the site settings UI categories. Nothing in the diff indicates these settings are “server-only with no admin UI”; lacking `client: true` would only affect exposure to the client, not whether admins can edit them in the admin settings UI.

adjudication_records.issue_text: PollFeed passes RSS content directly to TopicEmbed.import bypassing sanitization, allowing raw feed HTML (scripts/iframes) rendered unescaped in embed views

adjudication.rationale: In `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed`, the feed item HTML is taken from `i.content` and passed to `TopicEmbed.import` after only `CGI.unescapeHTML` and `.scrub` (no sanitization). `TopicEmbed.import` then creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true`, and `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` for `:raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. Finally, the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, so any scripts/unsafe HTML from the feed would be rendered unescaped in the embed output.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method raw_html option is exposed globally to any PostCreator caller, breaking the invariant that all posts pass the cooking pipeline

adjudication.rationale: The diff does introduce a new global bypass of the cooking pipeline: `Post#cook` now returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `PostCreator#setup_post` assigns `post.cook_method = @opts[:cook_method]` for any caller that passes it. This does break the prior invariant that posts always go through `post_analyzer.cook`/filters. However, the diff does not show any user-controlled path that can set `@opts[:cook_method]`; it’s currently used internally by `TopicEmbed.import` for RSS/remote imports. So it’s a legitimate API/safety/architecture concern, but not a verifiable functional defect on its own from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Happy-path-only spec for poll_feed leaves fetch, parsing, URL fallback, and import delegation untested; one malformed feed item kills the hourly poll with no retry

adjudication.rationale: The new `Jobs::PollFeed` logic does nontrivial work in `poll_feed` (network fetch `open(...)`, `SimpleRSS.parse`, per-item URL fallback `url = i.id if url.blank? || url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`, HTML unescape/scrub, and `TopicEmbed.import(...)` delegation), but `spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb` only tests the gating in `execute` and that it calls `poll_feed`, leaving the core behavior untested. Also, `poll_feed` has no per-item error handling and `sidekiq_options retry: false`; if an item lacks expected fields (e.g., `i.content` is nil so `i.content.scrub` raises) the job will error out for that run without retry. This is a concrete robustness/test-gap concern grounded in the diff, not a proven functional regression for all feeds.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve calls the entire Jobs::PollFeed job synchronously inside the request-serving job just to find one URL, causing full RSS feed re-imports on any embed lookup miss

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, it synchronously runs `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`) and `PollFeed#poll_feed` parses the entire feed and iterates `rss.items.each` importing each item. This can cause a full feed import attempt on any embed lookup miss before falling back to `fetch_http`. However, this is not clearly a correctness defect (uniqueness on `topic_embeds.embed_url` and `content_sha1` update logic reduce duplication), and it’s also not “inside the request-serving job” per this diff since `EmbedController#best` enqueues `:retrieve_topic` and renders `loading` rather than running retrieval inline.

adjudication_records.issue_text: The throttle in retrieved_recently? is bypassed by no_throttle: staff?, so a staff user browsing N pages fans out N full feed polls within the same minute

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently?`, throttling is explicitly bypassed when `@opts[:no_throttle]` is true (`return false if @opts[:no_throttle]`). The `Jobs::RetrieveTopic` job sets this option based on `user.try(:staff?)` (`TopicRetriever.new(args[:embed_url], no_throttle: user.try(:staff?)).retrieve`). When `perform_retrieve` runs and `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true, it triggers a full feed poll via `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` for each retrieval attempt. So a staff user can indeed cause multiple feed polls in a short period by triggering many retrievals, which is a concrete performance/architecture concern grounded in the diff, though not necessarily a functional correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method raw_html returns raw before the after_post_cook filter chain, so plugins like auto-embedding, mention/link rewriting, and spam heuristics never see imported content and cooked is stored unsanitized and identical to raw, later rendered via raw post.cooked

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `Post.cook_methods` and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, which bypasses `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` and the normal cooking pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` explicitly creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and feeds in HTML from RSS/remote sources (`i.content` / `Readability::Document#content`) without any sanitization shown here. The embed view then renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>`, and for `raw_html` posts `cooked == raw`. This makes imported content skip plugin processing (mentions/link rewriting/etc.) and be rendered as raw, potentially unsanitized HTML.

adjudication_records.issue_text: embed_url is matched by exact string equality between the JS-written discourseEmbedUrl and the RSS-written link with no shared canonicalization, so URL variant drift creates duplicate topics, duplicate comment threads, and an infinite 'Loading Discussion...' iframe reload

adjudication.rationale: The diff stores and looks up embeds by exact `embed_url` string: `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` does `where(embed_url: embed_url)` and `TopicRetriever`/`perform_retrieve` uses `where(embed_url: @embed_url).exists?`. Feed import (`PollFeed`) passes `i.link`/`i.id` directly into `TopicEmbed.import`, which persists `embed_url: url` unchanged. The JS embed iframe likewise passes `discourseEmbedUrl` verbatim as the `embed_url` param. There is no canonicalization/normalization (scheme, trailing slash, query, etc.), so URL variants will not match the stored row, leading to duplicate TopicEmbed rows/topics and to `EmbedController#best` repeatedly rendering `loading` and re-enqueueing `retrieve_topic`, causing the iframe to keep reloading (`loading.html.erb` reload loop).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Referer host comparison in embed_controller is exact-string against an unnormalized SiteSetting.embeddable_host, so mixed-case hosts fail equality and raise Discourse::InvalidAccess; TopicRetriever#invalid_host? has the same non-normalized comparison

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` the referer host is compared with exact string inequality: `URI(request.referer || '').host != SiteSetting.embeddable_host`. In `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` the same exact comparison is used: `SiteSetting.embeddable_host != URI(@embed_url).host`. The diff shows no normalization (e.g., `downcase`) of either side, so a mixed-case host in either the referer/embed URL or `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` would cause a false mismatch and raise/skip retrieval even though DNS hostnames are case-insensitive.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update path in TopicEmbed crashes with NoMethodError when embed.post is nil (deleted post), and because PollFeed has retry: false the whole feed import permanently stalls on subsequent items

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the update path assumes `embed.post` is always present: `post = embed.post` then `PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If the referenced post was deleted (no DB FK shown; only `post_id null: false`), `embed.post` can be `nil`, causing a runtime exception when trying to revise. In `Jobs::PollFeed`, the job iterates `rss.items.each` without rescuing exceptions, and `sidekiq_options retry: false` means a crash aborts processing remaining items for that run and won’t be retried by Sidekiq.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key (and its feed-modified: caching scheme) is dead code never called anywhere, creating a false assumption that conditional-GET caching exists

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the method `feed_key` defines a Redis-style cache key (`"feed-modified:#{Digest::SHA1.hexdigest(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)}"`) but it is never referenced by `execute` or `poll_feed`, and there are no other references to `feed_key` in the shown diff. This is dead code and could mislead readers into thinking a conditional-GET / modified-since caching mechanism exists when it does not.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No terminal failure state for the embed lifecycle: when retrieval can never succeed, the controller re-enqueues forever and the loading view reloads the iframe every 30 seconds indefinitely with no error signaling

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns nil, it unconditionally `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and renders `loading` (app/controllers/embed_controller.rb). The loading view forces `document.location.reload()` every 30 seconds (app/views/embed/loading.html.erb), so the iframe repeatedly hits `embed/best` and re-enqueues the job indefinitely if an embed can never be created (e.g., `TopicRetriever#invalid_host?` returns true when `URI(@embed_url).host` != `SiteSetting.embeddable_host`, so the job will never perform retrieval, or remote fetch/import fails with no persisted error state). There is no terminal/error state to stop reload/enqueue, so this can loop forever and continuously enqueue/execute jobs without user-facing failure signaling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import path silently changes API contract: --category/-c option removed, content now hardcoded to readability extraction and raw_html cook, topics created in default category with no way to select one, and created_at fidelity lost (all posts get current timestamp)

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the CLI option `--category/-c` is explicitly removed (deleted `method_option :category` and all `category_id` logic). The import implementation is changed from `PostCreator.new(... created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]), category: category_id)` to `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`, and `TopicEmbed.import_remote/import` do not accept or set `category` or `created_at`. As a result, imported topics/posts will use the default category and current timestamps, which is a verifiable behavior regression/data fidelity loss introduced by this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disqus import drops the --category/-c option and the category argument to PostCreator with no replacement, silently importing threads into the default uncategorized category

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor` the `--category/-c` option is removed and the `category_id` lookup/`PostCreator.new(..., category: category_id)` call is deleted. The replacement (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title])`) ultimately creates the topic via `PostCreator` in `TopicEmbed.import` without any category parameter. As a result, Disqus imports can no longer target a specified category and will create topics with no category set (defaulting to uncategorized behavior).

adjudication_records.issue_text: An already-shipped migration (create_top_topics) is modified to add force: true, which can silently drop the top_topics table and its rows on re-run, and modified shipped migrations never reach already-migrated installs causing code path divergence

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. Modifying an already-existing migration is a real review concern because it can create divergence between environments that have already run the original migration vs. fresh setups, and `force: true` can drop/recreate the table if the migration is executed against a DB where `top_topics` already exists (risking data loss). The claim that it was "already-shipped" isn't provable from the diff alone, but the risky modification itself is clearly present.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Spec asserts embed controller synchronously calls TopicRetriever in-process, but implementation enqueues a background job instead, so the spec fails and the documented 'embed fetched before response' behavior changed to a loading page without recording the drift

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it does `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, ...)` and `render 'loading'` (async), and does not instantiate `TopicRetriever`. However `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` asserts `TopicRetriever.expects(:new)... retriever.expects(:retrieve)` in that branch, so the spec will fail against this implementation. This is a real, diff-grounded correctness/test failure introduced by the change in control flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Post#cook returns raw for raw_html posts before applying the after_post_cook plugin filter, silently bypassing the plugin extension point for that class of posts

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes `Post#cook` to early-return `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (app/models/post.rb), which means `Plugin::Filter.apply(:after_post_cook, ...)` is not executed for those posts. This is a real, diff-grounded behavior change that can prevent plugins relying on `:after_post_cook` from running on imported/raw_html posts. It may be intentional (comment says to skip rendering pipeline), but it does bypass the plugin hook for that class of posts.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stored XSS: RSS/article content rendered as raw HTML with no sanitization via cook_method raw_html, executed on the Discourse origin

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a `cook_method` of `raw_html` (Post.cook_methods) and changes `Post#cook` to `return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, explicitly bypassing the normal cooking/sanitization pipeline. `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and uses untrusted remote/RSS content as `raw` (`TopicEmbed.import` called from `Jobs::PollFeed` using `i.content` and from `TopicEmbed.import_remote` using `doc.content` from `open(url)`). The embed view then renders `raw post.cooked` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`), which for these posts equals the stored raw HTML. There is no sanitization step shown for the imported HTML (RSS path is especially unsanitized), so this enables stored XSS executed on the Discourse origin.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No URL scheme filtering anywhere in the diff, so even the Readability allowlist permits javascript: URLs in href attributes

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces importing and rendering of remote HTML without any explicit URL-scheme sanitization. `TopicEmbed.import_remote` builds `Readability::Document` with an allowlist of tags/attributes including `a` and `href` (`lib/topic_embed.rb`), then `TopicEmbed.import` stores it as a post with `cook_method: :raw_html`, causing `Post#cook` to return `raw` directly (no cooking/sanitization) and the embed view renders it via `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (`app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). The only URL handling added is `absolutize_urls`, which rewrites leading-`/` links but does not filter schemes like `javascript:` in existing `href`/`src` values. Thus the finding about lack of scheme filtering for `href` is diff-grounded and represents an XSS/security defect risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: HTML attribute injection via unescaped url interpolated into the imported_from link, since url validation is only a prefix check that doesn't exclude quotes, angle brackets, or spaces

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, the `url` is only validated with `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//` and then interpolated directly into an HTML attribute and body: `link: "#{url}"` (server locale `embed.imported_from`). Since this is appended to `contents` and posts are created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` (so `Post#cook` returns `raw`), the resulting HTML is rendered without escaping (`raw post.cooked` in `app/views/embed/best.html.erb`). A crafted URL containing quotes/angle brackets/spaces could break out of the `href` attribute and inject arbitrary HTML/JS, making this a verifiable attribute injection/XSS risk introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Access control on /embed/best relies on a client-controlled Referer check, leaking restricted/private topic content without authentication

adjudication.rationale: `EmbedController#ensure_embeddable` authorizes access to `/embed/best` solely by comparing `URI(request.referer).host` to `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` (and otherwise does not require authentication), then renders a `TopicView` for whatever `TopicEmbed.topic_id_for_embed(embed_url)` returns. The `Referer` header is client-controlled/spoofable, so this check can be bypassed to access the endpoint (and view any embeddable topic) without coming from the intended host.

adjudication_records.issue_text: postMessage origin check in embed.js uses a substring test, allowing arbitrary origins containing the Discourse URL to drive the iframe
matched_golden_ids: The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe the same flaw: validating postMessage origins with a substring/indexOf check can be bypassed by attacker-controlled domains that merely contain the expected Discourse URL (e.g., evil-discourseUrl.com), allowing unauthorized origins to interact with the iframe.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Host equality check in topic_retriever.rb only matches hostname, allowing arbitrary ports on the embeddable host (and open-uri follows redirects), enabling SSRF

adjudication.rationale: In lib/topic_retriever.rb, invalid_host? only compares `SiteSetting.embeddable_host` to `URI(@embed_url).host`, ignoring scheme and port, so a URL like `http://allowed-host:1234/...` would pass the host check. The subsequent fetch path calls `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, @embed_url)` which does `open(url).read` (open-uri) without re-validating the final destination, so redirects/alternate ports are not constrained by the host check, creating an SSRF-capable request primitive within the new embed retrieval feature.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import with feed-controlled title and content uses skip_validations: true, bypassing rate limiting, spam, and length checks

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly bypasses validations and rate limiting for feed/remote-imported content. In `TopicEmbed.import`, new posts are created via `PostCreator.new(... skip_validations: true, cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html])` and updates use `PostRevisor#revise!` with `skip_validations: true, bypass_rate_limiter: true` (see `app/models/topic_embed.rb`). The title/content originate from RSS (`Jobs::PollFeed` uses `i.title` and `i.content`) or remote readability (`import_remote` uses `doc.title` / `doc.content`), so the finding that feed-controlled content bypasses length/validation and rate-limiter checks is directly supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb:11-26 — guard tests are tautological: each test stubs only one setting falsy while the other two default to falsy, so tests pass regardless of the guard's actual logic; must stub the other two settings to truthy values

adjudication.rationale: In Jobs::PollFeed#execute the guard is `feed_polling_enabled? && feed_polling_url.present? && embed_by_username.present?`. In spec/jobs/poll_feed_spec.rb the first three “requires …” tests stub only one setting to be falsy, but do not stub the other two to truthy. Given defaults in config/site_settings.yml (feed_polling_enabled: false, feed_polling_url: '', embed_by_username: ''), the guard will be false regardless, so `poll_feed` is never called even if one of the three conditions were accidentally removed or mis-implemented. The tests therefore don’t actually verify each individual guard condition as intended.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb:29-45 — spec never executes real TopicRetriever logic; the Redis setnx/expire throttle and perform_retrieve branches are stubbed out, so bugs like expiring the wrong key or inverted setnx truthiness would not fail any test

adjudication.rationale: In spec/components/topic_retriever_spec.rb, the “valid host” examples stub `retrieved_recently?` to return true/false and only assert whether `perform_retrieve` is called. That means the real throttle implementation in TopicRetriever#retrieved_recently? (the `$redis.setnx` + `$redis.expire` key logic in lib/topic_retriever.rb) is never exercised, so regressions like using the wrong Redis key or mishandling the setnx/expire behavior would not be caught by tests. This is a test coverage gap for newly added nontrivial logic, not a directly verifiable defect in runtime behavior from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb:40-52 — success context verifies mock wiring only: enqueued job arguments (user_id, embed_url), the loading template render, and the discourse_expires_in 1.minute cache header are all unasserted

adjudication.rationale: In `EmbedController#best`, when no `topic_id` is found it enqueues `Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...)`, renders the `loading` template, and always calls `discourse_expires_in 1.minute`. In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb` success context (around lines 40-52), the tests don’t assert any of those behaviors (job enqueue args, that `loading` is rendered on missing embed, or the cache expiry/header), so the finding is a specific, diff-grounded gap in test coverage rather than a functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb — the 'creates a topic view' test stubs TopicView.new and asserts the stub, so the embed page template never runs and has no test coverage

adjudication.rationale: In `spec/controllers/embed_controller_spec.rb`, the "creates a topic view when a topic_id is found" example sets an expectation on `TopicView.new` but does not `render_views`, so Rails controller spec defaults mean `app/views/embed/best.html.erb` is not executed. Additionally, the expectation does not provide a return value for `TopicView.new`, so even if views were rendered, `@topic_view` would be nil and the template would fail (`@topic_view.posts`). This leaves the embed page template effectively untested in this spec.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:44-46 — the update test only imports changed content; importing identical content (the no-revision branch) is untested, so a regression that always revises passes the spec

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import` (app/models/topic_embed.rb), the update path only calls `PostRevisor` when `content_sha1 != embed.content_sha1`; otherwise it should skip revising. The spec’s “Supports updating the post” example (spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:44-46) only exercises the changed-content branch by importing different contents, and there is no example importing identical contents to assert the no-revision branch (e.g., ensuring `PostRevisor` is not invoked / `updated_at` unchanged). This is a concrete, diff-grounded test gap for nontrivial logic, not a runtime defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb:37-38 — post.cooked == post.raw assertion is trivially true because both hold the same stored string, not because the markdown pipeline was skipped

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `Post#cook` explicitly returns `raw` when `cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `TopicEmbed.import` creates posts with `cook_method: :raw_html`. `post.raw` and `post.cooked` are distinct fields; their equality is not “trivially true” from storage alone, but is the expected outcome of the new raw-HTML cooking path. The finding overstates that the assertion is meaningless based solely on the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: lib/post_revisor.rb:85-86 — the skip_validations change is not pinned by any direct spec; no test calls PostRevisor#revise! with skip_validations: true on a post that would otherwise fail validation

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes PostRevisor#update_post to conditionally bypass validations (`@post.save(validate: !@opts[:skip_validations])`). There is coverage that *calls* this path indirectly (TopicEmbed.import updates via `PostRevisor#revise!(..., skip_validations: true, ...)` in `spec/models/topic_embed_spec.rb`), but no spec demonstrates the behavioral intent of the change: that a revise with `skip_validations: true` succeeds in a scenario where validations would otherwise fail. That leaves the new validation-bypass behavior unpinned by a targeted test for its critical edge case.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Adding force: true to already-shipped create_top_topics migration makes re-runs destructively drop the top_topics table and its production data

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes an existing migration `db/migrate/20131223171005_create_top_topics.rb` from `create_table :top_topics do |t|` to `create_table :top_topics, force: true do |t|`. In Rails, `force: true` will drop the table if it already exists before recreating it, which is destructive and can cause data loss if this migration is (re)executed against a DB that already has `top_topics` (e.g., inconsistent schema state or manual reruns).

adjudication_records.issue_text: force: true on new topic_embeds table drops embed rows on re-run while leaving topics/posts, causing duplicate topics to be created for the same embed URL

adjudication.rationale: The migration `CreateTopicEmbeds` uses `create_table :topic_embeds, force: true`, but Rails migrations are versioned and won’t “re-run” on an already-migrated database unless you explicitly rollback/reset. In normal operation, this won’t drop rows. Also, if you *do* rollback and re-migrate, the `topic_embeds` table would be dropped/recreated (losing embed rows) even *without* `force: true`, so the claimed duplicate-topic issue isn’t specifically caused by `force: true` as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: cook_method integer column has no DB check constraint, allowing silent drift between the column and the Enum that reclassifies posts and mangles raw HTML

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `posts.cook_method` as an unconstrained integer (`add_column :posts, :cook_method, :integer, default: 1, null: false`) and introduces an application-level enum mapping in `Post.cook_methods` (`Enum.new(:regular, :raw_html)`). There is no DB-level check constraint restricting valid values or enforcing the mapping, so invalid/out-of-range values (or future enum reordering) could be stored silently and change how `Post#cook` behaves (`return raw if cook_method == Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`). The claim about "mangling raw HTML" is somewhat speculative, but the lack of a constraint and potential for drift is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus import task silently drops the --category option, failing with 'Unknown option' and leaving imported topics uncategorized

adjudication.rationale: In `lib/tasks/disqus.thor`, the `method_option :category, aliases: '-c'` line is removed, along with all logic that looked up `category_id` and passed it into `PostCreator` (`category: category_id`). With this diff, running the task with `--category`/`-c` will cause Thor to reject the flag as an unknown option, and the new import path (`TopicEmbed.import_remote(...)`) does not set any category, so imported topics will be created uncategorized.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus import now reclassifies imported posts as raw_html and stores fetched content verbatim without markdown sanitization

adjudication.rationale: The diff changes Disqus import to call `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), which fetches remote HTML (`open(url).read`) and ultimately creates a post with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]` and `skip_validations: true` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). `Post#cook` now returns `raw` verbatim for `raw_html`, bypassing the normal cooking/rendering pipeline (app/models/post.rb), and the embed view renders it with `<%= raw post.cooked %>` (app/views/embed/best.html.erb). Additionally, RSS importing (`Jobs::PollFeed`) feeds `i.content` into `TopicEmbed.import` without any sanitization/filtering beyond `scrub`/`unescapeHTML`, so this can store and render arbitrary HTML from a feed, creating an XSS/security risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disqus import via import_remote fetches URLs over live HTTP, so dead or paywalled links return nil and silently skip entire threads that the old code imported unconditionally

adjudication.rationale: The Disqus import task was changed to create the OP post via `TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...)` (lib/tasks/disqus.thor), and `import_remote` does `open(url).read` over live HTTP (app/models/topic_embed.rb). Unlike the previous code path (PostCreator with a permalink), this now depends on the remote URL being reachable at import time; if the URL is dead/paywalled/blocked, `open` can fail (exception) or the import can return no post, causing `if post.present?` to skip importing the thread’s replies. This is a real behavioral regression introduced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TopicEmbed.import assumes embed.post is non-nil; a deleted post causes NoMethodError that permanently kills the scheduled PollFeed job and aborts remaining feed items

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, the update path does `post = embed.post` and then unconditionally uses it when `content_sha1` changes: `revisor = PostRevisor.new(post)` and `revisor.revise!(...)`. If the referenced post has been deleted (possible even though `topic_embeds.post_id` is non-null), `embed.post` will be nil and this will raise (e.g., inside PostRevisor), aborting the caller. Jobs::PollFeed iterates `rss.items.each` and calls `TopicEmbed.import(...)` without rescue; with `sidekiq_options retry: false` an exception would fail the job run and stop processing remaining items.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Single malformed feed item aborts entire poll: rss.items.each lacks per-item error handling and i.content can be nil (raises NoMethodError), with retry: false dropping remaining items silently

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, the loop `rss.items.each do |i|` processes items without any per-item rescue. It calls `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)`, but `i.content` can be `nil` for some feeds/items, which would raise `NoMethodError` on `scrub` and abort the whole job, preventing remaining items from importing. Additionally, `sidekiq_options retry: false` means the failed job won’t be retried, so subsequent items are skipped until the next scheduled run.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Throttle key set via redis setnx before retrieval is attempted, so failed fetches cause retries to no-op and the embed stays stuck on loading page forever

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#retrieve`, the throttle is applied via `retrieved_recently?` *before* `perform_retrieve` is called, and `retrieved_recently?` sets the Redis key (`$redis.setnx` + `expire 60`) when it decides the URL has not been retrieved recently. This means even if `perform_retrieve`/`fetch_http` fails, subsequent enqueued `RetrieveTopic` jobs within 60s will no-op due to throttling. However, the diff also shows the key expires after 60 seconds (`$redis.expire(retrieved_key, 60)`), so the “forever stuck” part is not supported by the code shown.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Timeout-less, size-unbounded outbound fetch using plain open-uri (no read_timeout/open_timeout or size cap) in TopicEmbed.import_remote and PollFeed

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces outbound HTTP fetches via plain `open-uri` without any timeouts or response-size limiting: `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` in `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb` and `open(url).read` in `TopicEmbed.import_remote` (`app/models/topic_embed.rb`). These can hang indefinitely or download unbounded data, creating a reliability/DoS risk in scheduled jobs and on-demand embed retrieval.

adjudication_records.issue_text: perform_retrieve calls PollFeed inline, so one embed request triggers a synchronous full-feed import, and a PollFeed failure silently skips the HTTP fallback

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicRetriever#perform_retrieve`, when `SiteSetting.feed_polling_enabled?` is true it calls `Jobs::PollFeed.new.execute({})` inline before attempting `fetch_http` (see `lib/topic_retriever.rb`), so an embed request can synchronously run a full feed poll/import. However, the claim that a PollFeed failure would "silently" skip the HTTP fallback isn’t supported by the diff: `perform_retrieve` does not rescue exceptions from `execute`, so a failure would more likely raise/abort rather than silently continue/skip.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Update branch crashes with NoMethodError when the embedded post has been deleted (embed.post is nil, no FK/dependent destroy), orphaning the embed row and poisoning the hourly poll

adjudication.rationale: In TopicEmbed.import, when an existing embed row is found, it does `post = embed.post` and then (on content change) `PostRevisor.new(post)` / `revisor.revise!` (app/models/topic_embed.rb). If the associated post record has been deleted, `embed.post` will be nil (no FK constraint shown; no dependent-destroy behavior is defined), so this path will raise (likely NoMethodError inside PostRevisor expecting a Post). Since Jobs::PollFeed calls TopicEmbed.import for each RSS item hourly, an orphaned topic_embeds row can repeatedly crash/abort feed polling for that URL.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-http feed items silently dropped with no log due to the url =~ /^https?/ regex check in import, producing zero topic and zero indication

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, non-HTTP(S) URLs are immediately ignored via `return unless url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, with no logging or error reporting. `Jobs::PollFeed#poll_feed` may still pass a non-HTTP(S) `i.id` when `i.link` is blank/invalid (`url = i.id if ... url !~ /^https?\:\/\//`), resulting in a no-op import and no indication to operators. This is a real, diff-grounded observability/edge-case concern, but the diff also suggests intentional scope to HTTP(S) URLs, so it’s not clearly a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: A bad embed_by_username silently disables feed polling entirely (return if user.blank? with no log)

adjudication.rationale: In the newly added feed polling job, `poll_feed` looks up the posting user via `User.where(username_lower: SiteSetting.embed_by_username.downcase).first` and then immediately `return if user.blank?` (app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb). That means a misconfigured `embed_by_username` causes feed polling to no-op with no logging/exception, making the feature appear “disabled” silently. This is an operational/diagnostics concern rather than a correctness defect in normal conditions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: feed_key is dead code: the modified hash Redis key is never stored or compared, implying a dropped If-Modified-Since optimization

adjudication.rationale: In `app/jobs/scheduled/poll_feed.rb`, `feed_key` is defined (building a Redis key `feed-modified:<sha1(url)>`) but it is never referenced anywhere in `execute` or `poll_feed`. The job always does `SimpleRSS.parse open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url)` with no conditional request or Redis compare/store, so the method is currently dead code and suggests an intended but unimplemented caching/If-Modified-Since-style optimization. This is not a functional defect by itself, but it is a concrete, diff-grounded issue (unused code / incomplete feature).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Resize messages silently ignored for older browsers where e.origin is undefined (indexOf coerces to 'undefined'), leaving the iframe clipped with no fallback height

adjudication.rationale: In `app/assets/javascripts/embed.js`, the resize handler uses `window.addEventListener('message', ...)`, which already excludes the “older browsers” implied by the finding (e.g., old IE without `addEventListener` would fail before even handling `e.origin`). The diff does not show any intended support path where `postMessage` works but `e.origin` is missing. Also, the iframe has no explicit height set, so it will fall back to the browser’s default iframe height rather than “no fallback height.”
